question: Should Microsoft Teams permanently support the proposed hybrid contract where root settings represent the legacy/default account and named accounts inherit shared root settings with account-specific identity and state?
rationale: The implementation is technically coherent and backward-preserving, but merging establishes long-lived semantics for configuration inheritance, environment variables, setup writes, credential selection, and persisted account state; repository policy requires explicit owner intent for that compatibility surface.

options.title: Approve the hybrid contract
options.body: Adopt root settings as supported shared/default-account configuration, retain legacy single-bot files, and land after the latest head is rebased and all exact-head checks pass.

options.title: Require accounts-only canonical config
options.body: Request a doctor-backed migration from shipped root credentials into `accounts.default` and remove steady-state dual-shape behavior before merge.

options.title: Pause multi-account support
options.body: Keep the existing single-bot contract until maintainers are ready to own the configuration, setup, credential, and state semantics.

recommendation.title: Approve the hybrid contract
recommendation.body: Adopt root settings as supported shared/default-account configuration, retain legacy single-bot files, and land after the latest head is rebased and all exact-head checks pass.

likelyOwner.reason: This account has the strongest recent feature and merger history across the Microsoft Teams channel and its adjacent configuration/runtime surfaces.
